name: Drinking water treatment; primary disinfection; gaseous chlorine; at plant
description:
This process reflects operation of the Primary Disinfection, Gaseous Chlorine drinking water treatment process normalized to the functional unit of 1000 cubic feet of treated drinking water. When part of the linked drinking water treatment system, this process "meets or exceeds [U.S.] National Primary Drinking Water Regulations for microorganisms, disinfectants, disinfectant by-products, inorganics, organics, and radionuclides."

To model the full scope of impacts associated with drinking water treatment - which includes acquisition, treatment, distribution and infrastructure - use one of the four drinking water processes:
• Drinking water; Chlorine disinfection; at consumer; ft3 drinking water
• Drinking water; Chlorine disinfection, no adsorption; at consumer; ft3 drinking water
• Drinking water; UV disinfection; at consumer; ft3 drinking water
• Drinking water; UV disinfection, no adsorption; at consumer; ft3 drinking water

Inventory data was collected from the Greater Cincinnati Water Works (GCWW) Richard Miller Treatment Plant, which serves a population of 241,000 customers and treats approximately 106 million gallons per day.
category: 22: Utilities/2213: Water, Sewage and Other Systems

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Data collected 2011. Drinking water treatment standards will change over time and with geography. Updating background electricity and input data should maintain process relevance so long as the target treatment system matches the defined system.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: The case-study facility is located in Cincinnati Ohio and this process reflects the topography and scale of that facility. Background datasets have been selected to represent U.S. average conditions.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: Inventory exchange values were sourced directly from the cited EPA report on disinfection options in municipal drinking water treatment. Background data sources have, in some cases, been updated to reflect newer and/or public data sources. Elementary flows were mapped to the federal elementary flow list.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: This process aggregates operational impacts. Infrastructure is included via upstream processes. No significant missing flows are known. The mass balance for this process was not calculated.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Primary data was provided by representatives of the Greater Cincinnati Water Works Richard Miller Treatment Plant.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Operational inventory values were provided by the case-study facility, in Cincinnati Ohio, per 1000 cubic feet of water treated.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: This drinking water unit process is part of a larger product system that models the full scope of flows necessary to estimate environmental impacts of drinking water delivered to the consumer. The scope of the model includes water acquisition, treatment, distribution and infrastructure processes. End-of-life disposal of infrastructure materials is excluded from the model scope. Primary data was provided by representatives of the Greater Cincinnati Water Works Richard Miller Treatment Plant. Uncertainty ranges are not available for this data.
processDocumentation.useAdvice:
This drinking water unit process is part of a larger product system intended to model the full scope of impacts associated with drinking water treatment - which includes acquisition, treatment, distribution and infrastructure. To model the full scope use one of the four drinking water processes:
• Drinking water; Chlorine disinfection; at consumer; ft3 drinking water
• Drinking water; Chlorine disinfection, no adsorption; at consumer; ft3 drinking water
• Drinking water; UV disinfection; at consumer; ft3 drinking water
• Drinking water; UV disinfection, no adsorption; at consumer; ft3 drinking water
These processes reflect the context of the case study community. Consider adapting background processes to your context if water treatment is a signficant source of impact within the scope of your assessment. Such adaptations could include substituting in an appropriate regional electricity grid or modifying the included treatment processes.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
This drinking water unit process is part of a larger product system intended for use as background data by LCA practitioners, industry and the general public. To model the full scope of impacts associated with drinking water treatment - which includes acquisition, treatment, distribution and infrastructure - use one of the four drinking water processes:
• Drinking water; Chlorine disinfection; at consumer; ft3 drinking water
• Drinking water; Chlorine disinfection, no adsorption; at consumer; ft3 drinking water
• Drinking water; UV disinfection; at consumer; ft3 drinking water
• Drinking water; UV disinfection, no adsorption; at consumer; ft3 drinking water

Data is sufficient to produce accurate LCIA results for all TRACI impact categories, energy demand, fossil depletion, and water use. 

Situation C2 - Accounting, without system-external interatctions. The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system excluding existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model.
